Inspect test results and flaky tests

## Usage

`circleci testresult <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command | Description                                       |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `flaky` | List flaky tests detected across a project's runs |
| `list`  | List test results for a job                       |

## Targeted Commands

| Command | Description                      |
| ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `get`   | Get a single test result by name |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with the test metadata CircleCI collects for a job, and with the
tests that flake across a project's runs.

When a job stores test results (via the 'store_test_results' step),
CircleCI parses them into per-test records. Use these commands to
review which tests failed, passed or were skipped without opening the
web UI.

toolCalls.name: circleci

List flaky tests detected across a project's runs

## Usage

`circleci testresult flaky [flags]`

## Flags

| Flag               | Description                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--jq string`      | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`)  |
| `--json`           | Output as JSON                                                                     |
| `--limit int`      | Maximum number of tests to show (0 = no limit)                                     |
| `--project string` | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                            |
| `--sort string`    | Sort by times_flaked or last_flaked (descending), or name (default "times_flaked") |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Flaky tests for the project in the current directory: 
  `circleci testresult flaky`
- The five worst offenders in another project: 
  `circleci testresult flaky --project gh/myorg/myrepo --limit 5`
- Names of tests that flaked more than five times: 
  `circleci testresult flaky --json --jq 'select(.times_flaked > 5) | .test_name'`

## Details

List the tests that failed and then passed within the same pipeline,
one row per test, most-flaked first. One call answers "which tests are
flaky?" — no need to walk runs and jobs. Job and workflow details are
those of each test's most recent flake.

JSON fields: test_name, classname, file, times_flaked, last_flaked_at,
job_name, workflow_name, job_id, workflow_id, run_id — one object per
line (JSONL).
[exit code: 0]

List recent runs for a project

## Usage

`circleci run list [flags]`

Aliases: `circleci run ls`

## Flags

| Flag                   | Description                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch string`  | Filter by branch                                                                  |
| `-B, --current-branch` | Filter by the currently checked-out branch                                        |
| `--jq string`          | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`               | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--limit int`          | Maximum number of runs to show [default: 10] (default 10)                         |
| `--project string`     | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                           |
| `--status string`      | filter by run status, e.g. success or failed                                      |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- List recent runs for the current project: 
  `circleci run list`
- Filter to the branch you have checked out: 
  `circleci run list --current-branch`
- Filter to a specific branch: 
  `circleci run list --branch main`
- List runs for an explicit project: 
  `circleci run list --project gh/org/repo`
- Show the last successful run: 
  `circleci run list --status success --limit 1`
- Output as JSON for scripting: 
  `circleci run list --json`

## Details

List recent runs for a CircleCI project.

A run is one execution of a pipeline. The project is inferred from the
current git repository's remote unless overridden with --project.

JSON fields: id, phase, outcome, current_outcome, branch, tag, revision, repository_url, commit.subject/url/author_name/author_login, created_at, warnings[].type/message/description/url

CircleCI found **3 flaky tests** in `gh/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli`. Each one flaked once, and all are in the `acceptance` package (`github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/acceptance`). A test counts as flaky when it failed and then passed within the same pipeline.

| Test | Times flaked | Last flaked (UTC) | Job / workflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TestRunnerResourceClassDelete_Interactive_Decline` | 1 | 2026-11-20 15:12 | `test-linux` / `ci` |
| `TestRunnerResourceClassDelete_Interactive_Decline/n` (subtest) | 1 | 2026-11-20 15:12 | `test-linux` / `ci` |
| `TestArtifact_Download` | 1 | 2026-11-17 19:10 | `test-windows` / `ci` |

**What this means:**
- In practice this is **2 separate problems**. The two `TestRunnerResourceClassDelete_Interactive_Decline` rows are a test and its `/n` subtest, and they flaked in the same job. The subtest failing probably made the parent test fail too.
- `TestArtifact_Download` flaked only on Windows (`test-windows`).
- Each test flaked only once, so none of them fails often yet.

**About the 30 days:** The flaky-test command can't filter by date, so I listed every flaky test it reports and checked the dates. The newest pipeline run I found was created on 2026-11-25. Assuming today is close to that date, both flake dates (Nov 17 and Nov 20) fall within the last 30 days. I couldn't get the actual current date, so I can't confirm the window exactly.

To look into a flake, use the IDs from the data: job `17fbba75-2ace-4a6b-88dd-f8e4586fa464` for the runner test, and job `b173a3c6-c6e4-4324-80dd-0b628ff42c20` for the artifact test.
